headline: Record sales, but fuel costs and investment losses bite
summary_short: Revenue rose 21.1% y/y to $20,186M, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 47% to $1.15 on higher fuel costs and a $218M investment loss; adjusted EPS was $1.72.
summary_long: Revenue grew 21.1% y/y to $20,186M, including $2,601M of third-party refinery sales; adjusted revenue rose 16% to $17,585M on flat capacity. Operating income fell 13.7% to $1,454M as fuel expense rose 69% and non-fuel unit costs rose 7.3%. GAAP EPS of $1.15 also reflected a $218M investment loss versus a $311M gain a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.72 versus $1.70. Free cash flow was $463M. Adjusted net debt fell to $13.4B. Guidance: December-quarter EPS $1.15-$1.65 and full-year EPS $5.10-$5.60.
confidence_notes: Source is the EX-99.1 press release inside the Oct 9 2026 8-K accession; resolve-edgar-exhibit.mjs found no EX-99 filename match, so the folder's non-cover candidate (deltaairlinesannouncessept.htm) was fetched directly. GAAP revenue includes third-party refinery sales that Delta strips out of adjusted revenue; GAAP and adjusted figures are not interchangeable. Q/q delta used for long-term debt since the company is paying down debt through 2026; other rows use y/y because airline results are seasonal. Company guidance ranges (December-quarter EPS, full-year EPS, free cash flow) were not persisted to the event's guidance[] array because no sanctioned script exists for that write.

drivers.explanation: Adjusted revenue rose 16% on flat capacity, driven by broad demand and healthy yield growth; premium revenue grew 18% and loyalty 18%. Third-party refinery sales of $2,601M also lifted GAAP revenue.
Fuel expense rose 69% on a 68% higher average fuel price, and non-fuel unit costs rose 7.3% on higher crew and revenue-related costs with capacity below plan, partly from summer storms.
Lower operating income plus a $218M net investment loss versus a $311M gain a year earlier swung non-operating results to a $380M expense.
Adjusted EPS of $1.72 was in line with last year despite more than $500M of higher fuel cost than guided in July; GAAP EPS also absorbed investment losses.
Delta made $1.2B of debt and finance lease payments in the quarter and plans to pay down more than $2B of debt in 2026.
CEO Ed Bastian said results show durability in an elevated fuel environment; the company expects roughly $4.5B of full-year pre-tax profit while absorbing a $6B fuel cost increase.
